newsitem.title: USA: Merrill Lynch pays $30 million to end California probe.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch pays $30 million to end California probe.

text.p: Merrill Lynch & Co. will pay about $30 million as part of an out-of-court settlement with the Orange County, Calif., district attorney's office, capping its 2-1/2 year criminal probe of the brokerage firm, sources said Thursday.
Under the settlement, the district attorney will close the investigation of Merrill Lynch and its employees, and will not to bring any legal action against them.
Merrill Lynch will deny any wrongdoing as part of the settlement, sources close to the probe said.
The district attorney plans to hold a news conference at 10 a.m. local time (1 p.m. EDT) to make the announcement. County prosecutors declined to comment in advance.
An Orange County grand jury has been investigating the roles played by various bond and investment firms, including Merrill Lynch, and other financial professionals in the county's bankruptcy crisis.
The grand jury focused on Merrill Lynch's role as the underwriter of county notes. The panel's deliberations have been kept secret, but rumours spread in recent weeks that indictments were likely.
Merrill Lynch declined to comment on the settlement.
Orange County shocked Wall Street in December 1994 when it filed for bankruptcy after losing more than $1.6 billion on risky investments. The county emerged from bankruptcy one year ago.
To recover the funds it lost, the county filed a $2 billion-plus lawsuit against Merrill Lynch, alleging it sold the county risky securities in violation of state law.
Merrill Lynch has denied any wrongdoing and has been contesting the county's lawsuit in court.
Sources said Merrill Lynch's settlement with the district attorney would not have any effect on the county's civil lawsuit against the brokerage firm.
The $30 million that Merrill Lynch will pay as part of the civil settlement will be deposited in the county's general fund, sources said.
